title: Reading connected clusters — full joining review
objectives: Student can read any 2–3 letter unvoweled cluster built from any combination of the 28 letters, correctly identifying each component letter regardless of its positional shape.
Student demonstrates the non-connector rule applying correctly and automatically, without needing the rule restated.
Student can read at least 30 real unvoweled Arabic words containing non-connectors, predicting each mid-word break before reading it.
Student's cluster-reading pace has visibly increased from lesson 1.7's baseline (informal, non-graded pacing check only).

slides.heading: Lesson 1.9 — Reading connected clusters: full joining review

audio.cue: ا: an open, unobstructed sound from deep in the chest cavity — no closure anywhere, just a clear open vowel
lips fully together
tongue-tip on gum ridge
tongue between teeth
ح: a strong, breathy, unvoiced friction from the middle of the throat — like fogging a mirror from deep in the throat, no English equivalent
خ: a rasping fricative from the upper throat/back of the tongue against the soft palate — a genuine back-of-throat 'kh', not softened
د: tongue-tip taps the upper gum ridge firmly — a plain, crisp 'd'
ذ: tongue-tip between the teeth, same point as ث but VOICED — 'th' as in 'this', never a 'z'

audio.title: Arabic101 Makharij Lesson 10 — ر (ra), the ULTIMATE guide

audio.cue: ز: tip of tongue near the lower teeth, a plain buzzing 'z' — voiced twin of س
س: tip of tongue near the lower teeth, a thin hiss — a plain 's'
ش: middle of tongue against the roof of the mouth, a soft 'sh'
ع: a mid-throat muscular squeeze, voiced — no equivalent sound in English or Turkic languages
غ: upper throat, same zone as خ but voiced — a uvular fricative, like a French uvular 'r'
ف: inner lower lip against the edge of the upper front teeth — a plain 'f'
ك: back of tongue against the soft palate, shallower in the mouth than ق — a plain 'k'
م: the two lips, with nasal resonance — 'm'
ه: a light, breathy throat release — a soft 'h', much gentler than ح
و: rounded lips — a consonant 'w'
ي: middle of tongue toward the roof of the mouth — a consonant 'y'

slides.heading: Everything you need to read any cluster
body: Rule 1 (lesson 1.7): a letter's sound never changes, but its SHAPE changes by position — isolated, initial, medial, final.
Rule 2 (lesson 1.8): 6 letters — ا د ذ ر ز و — never connect forward, no matter where they sit.
That's it. Those two rules are everything needed to read any connected cluster of the 28 letters.

slides.heading: Homework — 15–20 min/day
tasks: Re-read Reading sets A and B aloud (30 words), 2× through, predicting each non-connector break before you read it.
Re-read the 8 cold-read words daily until they are instant — these are the ones with no break at all.
Self-time the 12-word pacing set once a day and keep your own tally of which words felt hardest.
Write the positional forms of 2–3 tricky letters from today, 4 rows each in your notebook, saying the name and sound aloud as you write.
Bring your hardest-words tally to the start of lesson 1.10.

audio.cue: Read اسم right to left, letter by letter (alif + seen + meem), then blend: ism — “name”. No vowel marks yet: name each letter and the shape it took.
Read باب right to left, letter by letter (ba + alif + ba), then blend: bāb — “door”. No vowel marks yet: name each letter and the shape it took.
Read كتاب right to left, letter by letter (kaaf + ta + alif + ba), then blend: kitāb — “book”. No vowel marks yet: name each letter and the shape it took.
Read مسجد right to left, letter by letter (meem + seen + jeem + dal), then blend: masjid — “mosque”. No vowel marks yet: name each letter and the shape it took.
Read بحر right to left, letter by letter (ba + haa + ra), then blend: baḥr — “sea”. No vowel marks yet: name each letter and the shape it took.
Read رجل right to left, letter by letter (ra + jeem + lam), then blend: rajul — “man”. No vowel marks yet: name each letter and the shape it took.
Read قمر right to left, letter by letter (qaaf + meem + ra), then blend: qamar — “moon”. No vowel marks yet: name each letter and the shape it took.
Read شهر right to left, letter by letter (sheen + ha + ra), then blend: shahr — “month”. No vowel marks yet: name each letter and the shape it took.
Read وجه right to left, letter by letter (waw + jeem + ha), then blend: wajh — “face”. No vowel marks yet: name each letter and the shape it took.
Read نجم right to left, letter by letter (nun + jeem + meem), then blend: najm — “star”. No vowel marks yet: name each letter and the shape it took.
Read ملح right to left, letter by letter (meem + lam + haa), then blend: milḥ — “salt”. No vowel marks yet: name each letter and the shape it took.
Read صحن right to left, letter by letter (saad + haa + nun), then blend: ṣaḥn — “dish, plate”. No vowel marks yet: name each letter and the shape it took.

dailyChecklist: Read the 30 words in Reading sets A and B aloud, 2× through, predicting each break before reading.
Read the 8 cold-read words until they come without hesitation.
Self-time the 12-word pacing set once, and note which words were slowest.
Write the positional forms of 2–3 letters that gave you trouble, 4 rows each, saying each name and sound aloud as you write.

script: This is the Unit 1.2 consolidation lesson and the last full lesson before vowels. Nothing new is taught — everything today is transfer.
Restate the two rules once (slide 3) and then never restate them again. If the student needs the rule mid-drill, log it: that is a checkpoint risk.
Guided sets 1 and 2 deliberately mix distant shape-families so nothing can be guessed from alphabet order. Sets from lesson 1.7 were within-family; these are not.
Guided set 3 is prediction-first: student says where the joining will break before reading, then reads to confirm. Do not let them read first and rationalize after.
Reading sets A and B are the heart of the lesson — 30 real words, all containing non-connectors. This is the first time the student reads at real-word scale.
Run the cold read strictly: 8 genuinely unseen words, no prompting unless truly stuck. This is the single best predictor of Checkpoint 1 performance — log every hesitation.
Error-log review is done together, out loud, categorised (positional-shape / non-connector / sound-only). This feeds the Checkpoint 1 revision map directly.
Pacing check is encouragement framing only. If the pace has not moved since 1.7, that is data for you, not a message for the student.
Close on the vowels preview — the student should leave wanting lesson 1.10.
listenFor: Any letter from the high-risk six (ح, ض, ع, ق, the ذ/ز pair, ص) resurfacing as an error once embedded in a real word rather than read in isolation — the most diagnostic moment before Checkpoint 1.
Hesitation specifically at non-connector transitions — confirms whether lesson 1.8's rule is automatic or still consciously recalled.
Medial ـهـ and ـعـ misread inside real words even though the flashcard forms were correct in 1.7.
Student splitting a single word into two at a non-connector gap (reading بخار or تلميذ as two words).
Increasing hesitation as words grow from 3 to 4–5 letters — indicates letter-by-letter sounding rather than chunking. Normal here; note it for Phase 2 planning.
Reading pace on the cold-read set versus the rehearsed sets — a large gap means recognition is memorised, not decoded.
teacherNotes.homework: Reading sets A and B (30 words with non-connectors) aloud 2× daily with break-prediction, the 8 cold-read words until instant, one self-timed run of the 12-word pacing set, and positional forms of 2–3 tricky letters written 4 rows each.
